set.body:
TWO RESULTS FROM ONE BENCHMARK. The first refutes a claim I had been repeating; the second qualifies an API recommendation I made, including my own reasoning about why a convenience wrapper was safe.

SETUP: 216 voxels on a 6x6x6 grid, 216 searchlights, mean support 19 features, 4 conditions, 4 runs, 6 partition pairs, 80 timepoints per run.

RESULT 1 - THE 40x FIGURE IS WRONG. The field reviewer reported 28 plan executions taking 16.9 s against 0.41 s for the same 28 pairs on the identity-metric path, and I filed that as a performance concern to understand before surfacing crossnobis. Measured end to end:

  A  Euclidean geometry + rdm              0.746 s
  B  geometry, FIXED dense metric          1.131 s   1.5x
  C  crossnobis, LEARNED diagonal          1.446 s   1.9x
  D  crossnobis, LEARNED shrinkage         1.198 s   1.6x

The learned metric costs 1.6 to 1.9x the Euclidean path, not 40x. The reported gap was almost certainly an artifact of driving 28 SEPARATE plan constructions against one batched call, which measures the harness rather than the engine. I am withdrawing the performance concern I attached to bd-01KZYAV952F3MJFDWR43FH8XTV; nothing there argues against surfacing crossnobis.

RESULT 2 - THE COST STRUCTURES ARE OPPOSITE, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS.

  MATERIALIZED GEOMETRY               CROSSNOBIS PLAN
    geometry() build      0.731 s       plan_crossnobis() build  0.470 s
    contrast() #1         0.151 s       crossnobis() #1          1.145 s
    contrast() #2         0.027 s       crossnobis() #2          0.929 s
    rdm()                 0.026 s       crossnobis() #3          1.087 s

Geometry amortizes: pay once, then every subsequent question costs roughly 3 percent of the build. The crossnobis plan does not amortize at all - every query re-pays full price, flat across repeats.

This is CORRECT BEHAVIOUR and exactly what the documented query-first design says happens. It is not a defect.

BUT IT QUALIFIES MY OWN API PROPOSAL ON bd-01KZYAV8X93BX4VC13Z8PK8XRH, and I want the correction recorded next to the proposal. I argued that letting the verbs accept a relation and route query-first was safe, on the grounds that introduction.Rmd:331-333 asserts the values are identical to 1e-12 - so the plan/materialize distinction is about what an object RETAINS, not about the answer. That reasoning is right about VALUES and incomplete about COST.

A user who writes

  rdm(ev, at = searchlights(3), over = all_run_pairs(), metric = shrinkage_precision(0.2))
  contrast(ev, w1, at = searchlights(3), over = all_run_pairs(), metric = shrinkage_precision(0.2))
  contrast(ev, w2, at = searchlights(3), over = all_run_pairs(), metric = shrinkage_precision(0.2))

pays the full streaming cost three times, where the materializing path would have paid once and then answered twice nearly free. The unified verb hides a real and large economic difference behind an identical-looking call.

So the original concern I retracted was half right after all. I withdrew it as a SEMANTIC risk and that withdrawal stands - values are identical and the wrapper cannot lie about them. But there is an ECONOMIC version of the same concern that I did not consider and that survives: the distinction the wrapper hides is free semantically and expensive computationally.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION for the convenience verbs:
  keep them, because 1.6x is not a barrier and the ergonomic win is large
  but the one-liner form should be documented as the SINGLE-QUESTION path, with the
  materialized form shown as the answer for multiple questions on the same data
  and the print method for the returned view should say which path was taken, so a user
  asking three questions can see they paid three times
set.title: Measured: crossnobis is 1.6-1.9x Euclidean, not 40x, but it does not amortize across queries
